allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each integer n greater than 1, consider the function E(n,x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. Determine all real x that maximize E(n,x) among all real x, and determine the maximal value M(n) such that E(n,x) is less than or equal to M(n) for all real x, with equality for the maximizing x.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof is a direct unpacking of the definition of fractional part: frac(x)=x-floor(x) for every real x. It is complete, matches the lemma statement exactly, and uses only definition-level dependencies.
payload.previous_proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the fractional-part function frac, its value at x is x minus the greatest integer less than or equal to x, namely floor(x). Therefore frac(x) = x - floor(x), as claimed.
payload.role_in_assembly: Identifies the fractional part with the floor-remainder expression so that the inequality and equality lemmas can be rewritten into statements about frac(x).

payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, frac(x) = x - floor(x).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: The previous vetter feedback indicated that the proof was already a complete unpacking of the definition of frac. I retained that exact proof skeleton and made the justification explicit.
result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the fractional-part function frac, frac(x) is the difference between x and the greatest integer less than or equal to x, namely floor(x). Therefore frac(x) = x - floor(x).
result_payload.proof_summary: Immediate from the definition of the fractional part.
